 ~420px of enforced emptiness. Resetting the basis is the whole fix —
 never set flex-direction on an inherited flex container without checking
 what flex-basis meant before. */
 .lh-hero .lh-hero-text{flex:0 0 auto}
 .lh-hero .lh-portals--search{flex:0 0 auto}
 .lh-hero .lh-badge{margin-bottom:10px}
 .lh-hero .lh-title{margin:0 0 12px}
 .lh-hero .lh-subtitle{margin:0;max-width:52ch}
 .lh-hero .lh-trust-row{position:relative;z-index:1;margin:clamp(14px,1.8vw,22px) 0 0;gap:10px 24px}
 /* The bar itself carries the emphasis: taller, larger type, and a navy
 action instead of the yellow one — yellow reads promotional, and on warm
 paper it was the loudest thing in the hero. Scoped to .lh-herosearch so
 the same widget elsewhere keeps the brand button. */
 .lh-herosearch .sie-sps-bar{min-height:64px;padding:4px 6px 4px 14px}
 .lh-herosearch .sie-sps-input{font-size:17px}
 .lh-herosearch .sie-sps-btn{background:#12233D;border-color:#12233D;color:#fff;font-weight:600}
 .lh-herosearch .sie-sps-btn:hover{background:#1E3354;border-color:#1E3354}
 /* ── Results as a responsive grid, not a single strip ──────────────────
 .sie-res-list holds the program cards as direct children (verified live:
 18 cards, one parent, no headers in between), so one grid rule is enough.
 ⚠️ SCOPED TO THE HOMEPAGE ON PURPOSE. .sie-res-list is the shared
 SieFlowView markup — Leonardo renders into it too, with its own
 per-card animation offsets. Re-layouting it globally would change his
 results as a side effect of a homepage fix. */
 .lh-herosearch .sie-res-list{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fill,minmax(320px,1fr));gap:16px;align-items:start}
 .lh-herosearch .sie-res-list > .program-card{width:auto;max-width:none;margin:0}
 /* The flow view (AI matching on) groups results into one .sie-flow__branch
 per country. Each branch carries max-width:560px inside a 798px rail, so
 two never fit and they stack — the "single strip". Releasing the cap and
 tiling the branches gives two country panels per row at this width, and
 more on a wider screen, without touching the cards inside.
 ⚠️ Scoped to .lh-herosearch: Leonardo renders the same flow markup. */
 .lh-herosearch .sie-flow__branches{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fill,minmax(360px,1fr));gap:18px;align-items:start}
 .lh-herosearch .sie-flow__branch{max-width:none;width:100%}
 /* ── The figures strip ────────────────────────────────────────────────
 Serif numerals, monospaced labels, hairline rules, no card, no shadow,
 no colour fill behind each figure. The register of a register. */
 .lh-stats.lh-stats--figures{background:#F4F2ED;border-top:1px solid #E4E0D8;border-bottom:1px solid #E4E0D8;padding:0}
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stats-grid{max-width:1200px;margin:0 auto;padding:0 clamp(16px,4vw,48px);display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(4,minmax(0,1fr));gap:0}
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stat{padding:clamp(20px,2.4vw,32px) clamp(14px,2vw,28px) clamp(20px,2.4vw,32px) 0;border-right:1px solid #E4E0D8;text-align:left;background:none;border-radius:0;box-shadow:none}
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stat:last-child{border-right:0}
 /* Every cell except the first gets inner space on its left, so each rule
 sits with equal air on both sides instead of crowding the next figure.
 The first keeps padding-left:0 so its numeral lines up with the margin
 the hero headline uses. */
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stat + .lh-stat{padding-left:clamp(18px,2.4vw,34px)}
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stat-num{font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif;font-size:clamp(27px,2.9vw,40px);font-weight:600;letter-spacing:-.5px;line-height:1.05;color:#12233D;background:none;-webkit-text-fill-color:currentColor}
 /* #6B7A8D measured 3.92:1 against the warm band — under the 4.5:1 that
 11.5px text needs. The cool grey was fine on the old cold background and
 quietly failed when the palette warmed up; #4F5967 measures 6.2:1.
 Worth remembering when warming any other background. */
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stat-label{margin-top:8px;font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,monospace;font-size:11.5px;letter-spacing:1.3px;text-transform:uppercase;color:#4F5967}
 @media(max-width:700px){
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stats-grid{grid-template-columns:repeat(2,minmax(0,1fr))}
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stat:nth-child(2){border-right:0}
 }
 /* Monogram instead of a repeated building glyph. Hairline tile, serif
 letters — it reads as a placeholder somebody chose, not as missing data. */
 .lh-uni-logo-placeholder{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;background:#F4F2ED;border:1px solid #E4E0D8;border-radius:5px;color:#8A8578}
 .lh-uni-monogram{font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif;font-size:22px;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:1px;color:#12233D}
 /* ── For institutions ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
 The one full navy band on the page. It is dark on purpose: it marks a
 change of audience, so a student scrolling past knows at a glance that
 this part is not addressed to them. */
 .lh-inst{background:#12233D;color:#fff}
 .lh-inst-wrap *,.lh-inst-wrap *::before,.lh-inst-wrap *::after{box-sizing:border-box}
 .lh-inst-inner{max-width:1200px;margin:0 auto;padding:clamp(48px,6vw,88px) clamp(16px,4vw,48px);display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1.35fr) minmax(0,1fr);gap:clamp(28px,4vw,64px);align-items:start}
 .lh-inst-badge{margin:0 0 16px;font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,monospace;font-size:11.5px;letter-spacing:1.8px;text-transform:uppercase;color:#D7A83F}
 .lh-inst-h{margin:0 0 16px;font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif;font-size:clamp(26px,3.1vw,40px);line-height:1.16;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:-.5px;color:#fff;max-width:20ch}
 .lh-inst-body{margin:0 0 26px;font-size:clamp(15.5px,1.4vw,17px);line-height:1.65;color:#C6D2E0;max-width:54ch}
 .lh-inst-actions{margin:0;display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:12px}
 .lh-inst-btn{display:inline-block;text-decoration:none;background:#fff;color:#12233D;font-size:15.5px;font-weight:600;padding:14px 26px;border:1px solid #fff;border-radius:4px;min-height:44px}
 .lh-inst-btn:hover{background:#F4F2ED;color:#12233D}
 .lh-inst-btn--ghost{background:none;color:#fff;border-color:#44597A;font-weight:500}
 .lh-inst-btn--ghost:hover{background:none;color:#fff;border-color:#D7A83F}
 .lh-inst-terms{margin:0;padding:0;list-style:none}
 .lh-inst-terms li{border-top:1px solid #28405F;padding:20px 0}
 .lh-inst-terms li:first-child{border-top:0;padding-top:0}
 .lh-inst-k{margin:0 0 6px;font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,monospace;font-size:19px;color:#D7A83F}
 .lh-inst-v{margin:0;font-size:15px;line-height:1.6;color:#C6D2E0}
 @media(max-width:860px){
 .lh-inst-inner{grid-template-columns:1fr}
 }
 @media(max-width:900px){
 .lh-hero .lh-portals--search{grid-template-columns:1fr}
 .lh-herosearch .sie-res-list{grid-template-columns:1fr}
 .lh-herosearch .sie-flow__branches{grid-template-columns:1fr}
 .lh-heroalt{flex-direction:row;flex-wrap:wrap}
 .lh-heroalt-card{flex:1 1 220px}
 .lh-hero-scrim{background:linear-gradient(180deg,rgba(250,248,244,.97) 0%,rgba(250,248,244,.93) 62%,rgba(250,248,244,.72) 100%)}
 }
 /* ── Institutional pass, part 2 (2026-11-08, evening) ──────────────────
 Brings the sections below the hero onto the palette and type the hero
 already uses, so the page reads as one document instead of two designs
 stacked on top of each other. Everything here is homepage-only (it lives
 in this template) and is pure CSS: delete this block to revert. */
 /* The page itself: the site-wide body is cold pale blue (#E8F1FA), which
 showed through every transparent section (the institutions carousel and
 the study fields block) as a blue band between warm ones. */
 body.page-id-150{background:#FAF8F4}
 /* ⚠️ THE HEADLINE NEVER WAS SERIF. leonardo-homepage-css.min.css carries
 `.lh-wrap .lh-title{font-family:system-ui !important; font-size:44px
 !important; font-weight:800 !important; color:#003b73 !important}`, so
 the Source Serif rule earlier in this block lost on every device. Only
 !important with equal-or-higher specificity can beat it. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-hero .lh-title,.lh-wrap .lh-hero h2.lh-title{font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif !important;font-weight:600 !important;font-size:clamp(34px,4.4vw,58px) !important;line-height:1.08 !important;letter-spacing:-.6px !important;color:#12233D !important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#12233D !important}
 /* The accent word: italic navy reads editorial; bright orange read promo. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-hero .lh-gradient-text{color:#12233D;-webkit-text-fill-color:#12233D;font-style:italic;font-weight:600}
 /* One label above the headline is enough. The H1 eyebrow ("STUDY IN
 EUROPE") already does that job; the extra pill only added noise. */
 .lh-hero .lh-badge{display:none}
 /* Phones: the hero had no side gutter, so the eyebrow sat flush against
 the screen edge while the centred text did not. Left-aligned, with the
 same 20px gutter as the rest of the page, it matches the desktop. */
 @media(max-width:900px){
 .lh-hero .lh-hero-center{padding-left:20px;padding-right:20px;box-sizing:border-box;text-align:left}
 .lh-hero .lh-hero-text,.lh-hero .lh-subtitle{text-align:left}
 .lh-wrap .lh-hero .lh-title{text-align:left}
 .lh-hero .lh-trust-row{justify-content:flex-start}
 }
 /* ── Section headers: same voice as the institutions band ─────────────
 Serif headings and a small monospaced label instead of the rounded blue
 pills, which were the last "app" element on the page. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-section-header h2{font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif !important;font-weight:600 !important;font-size:clamp(28px,3vw,40px) !important;letter-spacing:-.4px;line-height:1.15;color:#12233D !important}
 .lh-wrap .lh-section-badge{display:inline-block;margin-bottom:14px;padding:0;background:none;border-radius:0;font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,monospace;font-size:11.5px;font-weight:500;letter-spacing:1.8px;text-transform:uppercase;color:#8C5A23}
 .lh-wrap .lh-section-sub{color:#4A525C}
 /* Section rhythm: paper / white / paper, so each block has an edge. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-how{background:#FAF8F4}
 .lh-wrap .lh-unis{background:#fff;border-top:1px solid #E4E0D8}
 .lh-wrap .lh-dest-section--origins{background:#fff;border-top:1px solid #E4E0D8}
 /* How it works: the three steps were top-aligned, so the middle card
 (longer text) hung lower than its neighbours. Stretch evens them. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-steps{align-items:stretch}
 .lh-wrap .lh-step{background:#fff;border:1px solid #E4E0D8;border-radius:6px;box-shadow:none}
 .lh-wrap .lh-step-num{background:#12233D;font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,monospace;font-weight:500}
 .lh-wrap .lh-step-icon{background:#F4F2ED;color:#12233D;border-radius:6px}
 .lh-wrap .lh-step-arrow{color:#B7B1A5}
 /* Cards: tighter corners and hairlines everywhere. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-uni-card{border-radius:6px;box-shadow:none}
 .lh-wrap .lh-dest-section--origins a[class*="card"],.lh-wrap .lh-dest-section--origins [class*="card"]{border-radius:6px;border-color:#E4E0D8;box-shadow:none}
 .lh-wrap .lh-dest-section--countries a[class*="card"],.lh-wrap .lh-dest-section--countries [class*="card"]{border-radius:6px}
 /* ── Study fields block (rendered by [sie_study_fields] after .lh-wrap) ─
 Six bright category colours, gradient pills and a gradient CTA made it
 the loudest part of the page. Same content, one navy, warm neutrals.
 The branch colours arrive as INLINE custom properties and inline
 backgrounds, so these overrides need !important to apply. Scoped to the
 homepage: the study-field pages keep their colour coding. */
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-title{font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif;font-weight:600;font-size:clamp(28px,3vw,40px);letter-spacing:-.4px;color:#12233D}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-subtitle{color:#4A525C}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__source-pill{background:#12233D !important;background-image:none !important;box-shadow:none !important;border-radius:4px}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__junction-dot{background:#12233D}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__branch{--branch-color:#12233D !important;--branch-bg:#F4F2ED !important;border:1px solid #E4E0D8;border-radius:6px;box-shadow:none}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__branch-accent{display:none}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__branch-icon{background:#12233D !important;border-radius:5px}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__branch-count{background:#F4F2ED !important;color:#12233D !important}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__field-card{background:#FAF8F4;border:1px solid #EDEAE3;border-radius:5px}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__field-card:hover{border-color:#12233D}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__field-icon{background:#F4F2ED !important;color:#12233D !important;border-radius:5px}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__leo-link{color:#0B5FA5 !important}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-leonardo{background:#12233D !important;background-image:none !important;border-radius:6px}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-leo-btn{background:#fff !important;color:#12233D !important;border-color:#fff !important;border-radius:4px}
 /* Alignment: the search widget carries its own 24px side padding, so the
 bar sat indented from the headline above it; and the trust row was
 centred under a left-aligned column. Both now share the text's edge.
 Only the LEFT padding goes: removing the right one too pushed the
 "AI-enhanced matching" toggle across the seam into the navy side. */
 .lh-herosearch .sie-sps-wrap{padding-left:0 !important}
 .lh-hero .lh-trust-row{justify-content:flex-start}
 /* Institution cards: the stylesheet tints each card top a different pastel
 (blue / yellow / blue) via !important rules at .lh-uni-card:nth-child()
 specificity, so this needs one more class to win. Plain paper, so the
 monogram or logo is the only thing that differs between cards. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-uni-card:nth-child(n) .lh-uni-card-top{background:#F4F2ED !important;background-image:none !important;border-bottom:1px solid #EDEAE3}
 .lh-wrap .lh-uni-cta{color:#0B5FA5 !important}
 .lh-wrap .sie-dest-hub__name{color:#12233D}
 /* Europe silhouette on the navy side. Present, never loud: a lighter blue
 at 15% so the copy on top keeps full contrast. The right edge fades out

 hairline seams between neighbouring countries; opacity sits on the <svg> itself so overlapping strokes cannot add up into darker lines. */

 DESTINATIONS PANEL  — overlay + grid
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
 /* Outer layer: covers full viewport */
 .sie-dest-panel {
 position: fixed;
 inset: 0;
 z-index: 2147483000;
 display: flex;
 align-items: stretch;
 justify-content: flex-end;
 opacity: 0;
 visibility: hidden;
 pointer-events: none;
 transition: opacity .25s ease, visibility .25s;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel.open {
 opacity: 1;
 visibility: visible;
 pointer-events: auto;
 }
 /* Backdrop */
 .sie-dest-panel__backdrop {
 position: absolute;
 inset: 0;
 background: rgba(11, 55, 112, .52);
 backdrop-filter: blur(3px);
 -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(3px);
 cursor: pointer;
 }
 /* Sheet — right-panel on desktop */
 .sie-dest-panel__sheet {
 position: relative;
 z-index: 1;
 width: min(800px, 100%);
 height: 100%;
 background: #fff;
 overflow-y: auto;
 -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch;
 padding: 26px 26px 40px;
 display: flex;
 flex-direction: column;
 gap: 0;
 transform: translateX(28px);
 opacity: 0;
 transition: transform .38s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1), opacity .38s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1);
 box-shadow: -20px 0 48px rgba(0,0,0,.18);
 }
 .sie-dest-panel.open .sie-dest-panel__sheet {
 transform: translateX(0);
 opacity: 1;
 }
 /* Mobile: bottom-sheet */
 @media (max-width: 767px) {
 .sie-dest-panel {
 align-items: flex-end;
 justify-content: stretch;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__sheet {
 width: 100%;
 height: 92vh;
 border-top-left-radius: 22px;
 border-top-right-radius: 22px;
 padding: 20px 16px 40px;
 transform: translateY(28px);
 box-shadow: 0 -16px 48px rgba(0,0,0,.18);
 }
 .sie-dest-panel.open .sie-dest-panel__sheet {
 transform: translateY(0);
 }
 }
 /* ── Header ── */
 .sie-dest-panel__header {
 display: flex;
 align-items: center;
 justify-content: space-between;
 margin-bottom: 6px;
 flex-shrink: 0;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__titlewrap {
 display: flex;
 align-items: center;
 gap: 10px;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__globe {
 font-size: 22px;
 color: #1e66f5;
 line-height: 1;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__title {
 font-size: 1.5rem;
 font-weight: 800;
 color: #0b3770;
 margin: 0;
 line-height: 1.2;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__close {
 background: transparent;
 border: 0;
 font-size: 22px;
 color: #0b3770;
 cursor: pointer;
 padding: 6px 8px;
 border-radius: 8px;
 line-height: 1;
 opacity: .75;
 transition: opacity .15s, background .15s;
 flex-shrink: 0;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__close:hover {
 opacity: 1;
 background: #f0f4ff;
 }
 /* Subheading */
 .sie-dest-panel__sub {
 color: #466087;
 font-size: .94rem;
 margin: 0 0 20px;
 flex-shrink: 0;
 }
 /* ── Country grid ── */
 .sie-dest-panel__grid {
 display: grid;
 grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr);
 gap: 14px;
 /* allow this to grow and scroll */
 flex: 1;
 align-content: start;
 }
 @media (max-width: 620px) {
 .sie-dest-panel__grid {
 grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr);
 gap: 10px;
 }
 }
 @media (min-width: 621px) and (max-width: 860px) {
 .sie-dest-panel__grid {
 grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);
 }
 }
 /* ── Country card ── */
 .sie-dest-panel__card {
 position: relative;
 display: block;
 aspect-ratio: 3 / 2;
 border-radius: 12px;
 overflow: hidden;
 text-decoration: none;
 background: #1d3557;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__card--no-img .sie-dest-panel__card-bg {
 background: linear-gradient(135deg, #1d3557 0%, #1e66f5 100%);
 }
 /* Hero image layer — scales on hover */
 .sie-dest-panel__card-bg {
 position: absolute;
 inset: 0;
 transition: transform .4s ease;
 will-change: transform;
 }
 /* <img> fills the card exactly like background-size:cover did.
 loading="lazy" means the browser only fetches each image when the
 panel opens and the card enters the viewport — saving ~30 MB of
 upfront image requests on every page that includes this panel. */
 .sie-dest-panel__card-img {
 position: absolute;
 inset: 0;
 width: 100%;
 height: 100%;
 object-fit: cover;
 object-position: center;
 display: block;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__card:hover .sie-dest-panel__card-bg,
 .sie-dest-panel__card:focus-visible .sie-dest-panel__card-bg {
 transform: scale(1.07);
 }
 /* Gradient overlay + text */
 .sie-dest-panel__card-body {
 position: absolute;
 inset: 0;
 display: flex;
 flex-direction: column;
 justify-content: flex-end;
 padding: 10px 12px 10px;
 background: linear-gradient(
 to top,
 rgba(0, 0, 0, .72) 0%,
 rgba(0, 0, 0, .30) 55%,
 transparent 100%
 );
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__card-name {
 color: #fff;
 font-weight: 700;
 font-size: .92rem;
 line-height: 1.2;
 text-shadow: 0 1px 5px rgba(0,0,0,.55);
 display: block;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__card-arrow {
 display: block;
 color: rgba(255,255,255,0);
 font-size: .75rem;
 margin-top: 2px;
 transition: color .2s ease, transform .2s ease;
 line-height: 1;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__card:hover .sie-dest-panel__card-arrow,
 .sie-dest-panel__card:focus-visible .sie-dest-panel__card-arrow {
 color: rgba(255,255,255,.9);
 transform: translateX(4px);
 }
 /* ── Body-scroll lock ── */
 body.sie-dest-panel-open {
 overflow: hidden;
 }
 /* ── Country interest heart ── */
 .sie-country-heart {
 position: absolute;
 top: 8px;
 right: 8px;
 z-index: 10;
 background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.88);
 border: none;
 border-radius: 20px;
 padding: 4px 8px 4px 7px;
 display: flex;
 align-items: center;
 gap: 4px;
 cursor: pointer;
 font-size: 13px;
 color: #94a3b8;
 box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.22);
 backdrop-filter: blur(6px);
 -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(6px);
 transition: color .18s, transform .18s, background .18s;
 line-height: 1;
 min-width: 28px;
 justify-content: center;
 }
 .sie-country-heart:hover {
 transform: scale(1.12);
 background: #fff;
 color: #ef4444;
 }
 .sie-country-heart.voted {
 color: #ef4444;
 background: #fff;
 }
 .sie-country-heart.voted i {
 animation: sie-heart-pop .35s cubic-bezier(.36,.07,.19,.97);
 }
 @keyframes sie-heart-pop {
 0%   { transform: scale(1); }
 40%  { transform: scale(1.45); }
 70%  { transform: scale(.88); }
 100% { transform: scale(1); }
 }
 .sie-country-heart__count {
 font-size: 11px;
 font-weight: 700;
 color: inherit;
 display: none;
 }
 .sie-country-heart.has-votes .sie-country-heart__count {

 }
 /* ── Trigger button styles (for use in any menu) ── */
 /* Desktop globe icon */
 .se-dest-desktop-btn {

 background: transparent;
 border: 0;

 }
 .se-dest-desktop-btn:hover {
 transform: scale(1.15);
 color: #FFCC00;

 /* Tooltip on desktop */
 @media (min-width: 1024px) {
 .se-dest-desktop-btn::after {

 .se-dest-desktop-btn:hover::after {
 opacity: 1;

 }

 background: #1e66f5 !important;

<div class="ecl"><h2><strong>What is the Conference?</strong></h2>

<p>The <strong>Conference on the Future of Europe </strong>is the first transnational discussion with Europeans on how to address Europe’s challenges together. This is an opportunity to think about what citizens and&nbsp; civil society want for the European Union.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

  <div class="eac-body lc-stripe-wrapper-text"><h2><strong>How does the Conference work?</strong></h2>

<p>Europeans can share ideas via the <a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/?locale=en" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">Multilingual Digital Platform</a>, and both national and&nbsp;<a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/assemblies/citizens-panels" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">European Citizens' Panels</a>. These contributions feed into the&nbsp;<a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/pages/plenary" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">Conference Plenaries</a>.</p>

<p>The Conference&nbsp;offers a new public forum for an open, inclusive, and transparent debate with citizens around a number of key priorities and challenges.</p>

<h2><strong>How can you participate?</strong></h2>

<ul>
	<li><!--[if !supportLists]--><!--[endif]--><a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/processes?locale=en&amp;pk_source=pdf_document&amp;pk_medium=link&amp;pk_campaign=europarl" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">share your own ideas or support others’ ideas</a> on the multilingual digital Conference platform</li>
	<li><!--[if !supportLists]--><!--[endif]-->organise your own events and promote it by adding them to the <a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/?locale=en&amp;pk_source=pdf_document&amp;pk_medium=link&amp;pk_campaign=europarl" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">Conference platform</a></li>
	<li><!--[if !supportLists]--><!--[endif]-->take a look at the <a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/meetings" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">events organised by people across the EU</a></li>
</ul>

<h2><strong>What will the outcome be?</strong></h2>

<p>All of the ideas gathered and reports on events are published on the platform openly and transparently. These reports will then directly influence the discussions in the European Citizens’ Panels as well as in the Plenaries, where citizens will enter into a dialogue with national and European decision makers.</p>

<p>By spring 2022, the Conference will provide guidance on the future of Europe to the European institutions</p>

<p><a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/pages/getinvolved" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">Get involved and make your voice heard when it comes to education, culture, youth, sport, and more</a>.</p>

<p>Follow on Twitter at&nbsp;</p>

<ul>

</ul>

Dein Part in unserem Team.
Tätigkeiten.

Qualifikation

Dein Profil.

Einen tadellosen Lebenslauf und Bestnoten? Das ist gut und wird bei uns auch honoriert, muss aber nicht sein. Wir interessieren uns vor allem für dich als Menschen und prüfen immer individuell, ob deine Erwartungen, deine Skills und dein Drive zu uns passen. Eigenschaften wie selbstständiges Arbeiten, ein hoher Qualitätsanspruch, Ownership und Aufgeschlossenheit gegenüber Neuem solltest du dabei auf jeden Fall mitbringen.

Zusätzlich sind folgende Eigenschaften für deine Stelle von Relevanz.

Benefits

Warum wir kein normaler Arbeitgeber sind.
Unser Profil.

Ja, wir fordern einiges von unseren Teammitgliedern, dafür haben wir aber auch einiges zu bieten. Wir vertrauen den Menschen, mit denen wir zusammenarbeiten und schaffen ein Umfeld, in dem sich jeder gemäß seinen individuellen Stärken und Schwächen weiterentwickeln kann. Wer hoch hinaus möchte, bekommt früh viel Verantwortung und Entwicklungschancen, wer sich noch unsicher ist, wo es hingehen soll, wird an die Hand genommen und erhält Orientierung. Wir sind keine Chefs, Mitarbeiter und Praktikanten, wir sind ein eingeschworenes Team, das zusammen an einem Strang zieht.

Darüber hinaus kannst du dich bei uns auf die folgenden Punkte freuen:

  • Attraktive Vergütungschancen und durchlässige Karrierestrukturen – bei uns bestimmen dein Einsatz und deine Leistung deinen künftigen Karriereweg

  • Eine steile Lernkurve als echter Benefit statt Buzzword – bei uns kümmern sich engagierte Mentoren von renommierten Unternehmensberatungen und Universitäten um deine Entwicklung

  • Arbeit mit Impact – profitiere von direktem Austausch mit Geschäftsführern unserer mittelständischen Kunden und arbeite so an Themen, die wirklich zügig und gewinnbringend umgesetzt werden

  • Flexibilität, die du dir verdienst – deine gute Arbeit wird nicht nur finanziell wertgeschätzt. Wir geben dir auch mit individuellen Home-Office-Möglichkeiten die Freiheiten, die du benötigst

  • Das passende Umfeld – ob „State of the Art“ in Sachen Ausstattung mit Laptop, Firmenhandy, höhenverstellbaren Tischen oder coolen Teamevents wie zuletzt z.B. Workation in Barcelona und Griechenland, Golfen oder Kochkursen. Bei TaxIt macht die Arbeit noch Spaß

  • Mehr von deinem Brutto – wir sorgen mit Zusatzleistungen wie einem Deutschlandticket, einem monatlichen 50€ Einkaufsgutschein oder der Fitnessstudiomitgliedschaft (Urban Sports Club) für mehr Netto vom Brutto auf deinem Konto

Bewerbungsprozess.

Es gibt Chancen im Leben, die man nicht verpassen sollte. Das ist eine davon. Schicke uns jetzt deine Bewerbung über das digitale Bewerbungsformular und lerne uns persönlich kennen.

Wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung und melden uns zeitnah bei dir. 🚀

We're looking for a Senior Integrated Campaign Manager, Brand & GTM to join our Integrated Marketing team at Pleo. In this role, you'll help architect, roll out, project manage, and drive the Go-To-Market (GTM) execution for our major 2027 brand marketing strategy and campaigns and be part of turning brand strategy, positioning, and creative concepts into operational GTM blueprints as we scale our multi-segment (SMB, Mid-Market, Enterprise) reach across 6 key European markets. If you're excited about high-visibility, full-funnel orchestration and balancing long-term brand equity building with full-funnel conversion, and are passionate about integrated brand and GTM marketing in high-growth B2B SaaS, then this is the opportunity for you!

Who you’ll be working with and reporting to

You’ll report to our Director of Integrated Marketing and work closely with teams in Brand Marketing, Digital, Field/Events, Content, PR, Product Marketing (PMM), Marketing Ops, Data, and Sales/Growth channels. Our team is highly collaborative and dedicated to bridging top-of-funnel brand awareness with lower-funnel acquisition, ensuring every campaign moment translates into market salience, customer engagement, and measurable business impact. You’ll also have the chance to partner with teams across country teams, local market stakeholders, Sales Leadership, SDRs, and Field squads to ensure success.

What you’ll be doing

As a Senior Campaign Manager, you will:

  • Integrated GTM Architecture & Strategic Planning: Translate the overarching 2027 brand strategy into actionable, full-funnel GTM campaign blueprints across SMB, Mid-Market, and Enterprise segments, architecting campaign flighting and distribution models across 6 European markets.

  • The "Master Brief" & Cross-Functional Squad Leadership: Own and author comprehensive Integrated Campaign Master Briefs, leading the operational rhythm of cross-functional squads to execute multi-channel strategies (OOH, Paid Social, VIP activations, Digital, ABM) on time and within scope.

  • Localization & Regional Adaptation: Partner with country teams and local market stakeholders to ensure master campaign frameworks balance global consistency with local relevance and execution precision.

  • Strategic Brand Partnership & Enablement: Serve as the strategic execution peer to the Brand Marketing Lead, while partnering with Sales Leadership, SDRs, and Field teams to equip customer-facing squads with the stories, tools, and campaign momentum needed to capitalize on campaign-generated intent.

What you bring

  • A proven track record leading multi-million dollar, multi-country, full-funnel integrated campaigns in high-growth B2B SaaS or tech environments.

  • Deep experience taking high-level brand frameworks and translating them into multi-channel GTM blueprints across varied audience segments (SMB to Enterprise).

  • High proficiency in aligning cross-functional teams (Creative, Digital, PR, Ops, Sales) and holding squads accountable to tight deadlines and complex campaign launches.

  • Deep understanding of how to run campaigns across diverse European markets, with a clear perspective on modular campaign design and local adaptation.

  • A background in integrated marketing, GTM campaign management, or brand marketing orchestration within B2B technology or SaaS.

  • You thrive as the operational bridge between high-level brand strategy and lower-funnel demand generation, turning concepts into structured GTM blueprints.

About Zable

Zable (formerly Lendable) is on a mission to build the world's best technology to help people get credit and save money.

  • Founded in 2014, profitable since 2017, unicorn since 2021

  • The number one issuer of new credit cards and loans in the UK

Zable was founded on the belief that smarter technology is the solution to lower cost, more transparent consumer finance. Our proprietary foundation models analyse thousands of data points in seconds, drawing a more complete picture of individual financial behaviour. This means we can make better risk decisions, widening access and lowering prices.

The Zable credit card harnesses this technology to deliver better borrowing for three million people. Through our superapp, Zable connects this card to a single platform which makes it effortless to manage credit, get a loan, refinance existing borrowing, switch utilities, get a mobile plan and save more.

Zable is now the number one issuer of new credit cards and personal loans in the UK, but we’ve barely got started. Next, we’re taking our approach to some of the biggest markets in the world - the US and Mexico - where hundreds of millions of people are underserved by outdated bank processes.

Join us if you want to

  • Take ownership across a broad remit - you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Zable from day one

  • Work in small teams of exceptional people - who are relentlessly resourceful to solve problems and find smarter solutions than the status quo

  • Build the best technology in-house - using new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting

 

We're looking for an experienced and proactive Senior Product Designer to join our Product Design team at Zable. You'll join a team of 5 product designers and report to the VP of Product & Design.

You'll work mainly on the Zable app, our financial SuperApp with 2M+ monthly active users. It brings together credit cards, loans, memberships, mobile and more in one place. You'll own complex product areas end-to-end, from discovery and research through to polished, production-ready design. You'll set design direction alongside PMs and Engineering, mentor other designers, and help raise the bar for craft and outcomes across the team.

The ideal candidate

  • 5+ years of product design experience, ideally in fintech or a fast-paced startup

  • Strong mobile app and web experience

  • Customer-obsessed and data-literate: you challenge solution-led briefs and back decisions with evidence

  • Takes real creative risks, and can bring a team along with a clear story for why a bolder direction is right

  • Confident with senior stakeholders, and pushes back when quality or customer outcomes are at risk

  • AI-native: you push past the first obvious output, not just work faster

  • Enjoys raising the bar for other designers through mentoring and feedback

    • Designing AI-powered products (explainability, human override)

    • Shipping improvements without engineering, e.g. via CMS or no-code tools

    • Regulated environments, e.g. Consumer Duty

    • UX writing

What you'll be doing

  • Lead discovery, choosing the right research method and turning findings into clear design direction

  • Own design delivery for your squad, from first flows through to build

  • Work with engineers throughout design, not just at handoff, weighing build cost in your decisions

  • Contribute to the design system, and know when breaking from it is right for the customer

  • Run usability tests and experiments with clear measures of success

  • Use AI across your workflow, including pushing design changes to production yourself

  • Design to Consumer Duty and accessibility standards, and call out issues in others' work

  • Run design critiques and write rationale that stands on its own

Our design principles

  1. Simplicity wins

    1. If a user has to think too hard, we’ve already lost. We strip away complexity, jargon, and unnecessary steps to make managing finances effortless. Every screen should feel intuitive, focused, and frictionless.

  2. Evidence over ego

    1. We don’t design based on opinions. Everything we build is informed by data, tested, and refined based on real user behavior.

  3. Trust is our best feature

    1. Finance is built on trust. Every design decision should reinforce transparency, security, and user confidence. We prove we care by helping users make financial decisions that empower them.

Who We Are

Zefir is building an AI autopilot for home sales in Europe, starting in France. Our agent runs each sale from listing to closing. It coordinates buyers, sellers, and local brokers, manages listings across property portals, and handles the paperwork. We help homeowners sell for the best price on a timeline that works for them.

We’ve raised €60 million from Sequoia Capital and other leading investors. Our goal is to help millions of Europeans take the next step in their lives, whether that means moving to a new city for work or making room for a growing family.

The mission

Zefir sells homes with an AI agent, but our growth is still run mostly by hand.

Every week, someone reads the dashboards, works out why bookings dropped on Tuesday, moves budget from one channel to another, asks for new creatives and fixes a broken tracking tag. Each of these tasks follows rules we could write down. Your job is to write them down and hand them to agents: software that watches the funnel all day, explains what changed and makes the routine fixes itself, within limits the team sets.

You'll learn those rules by doing the work first. From day one you run our acquisition: around €1M of spend a month on Meta, Google and new channels, in a business growing about 2.5x a year. The number you answer for is the expected margin of each call we book. Cheap leads that never become sellers don't count. Anything you still do by hand after six months is a task you haven't automated yet.

Few places let you try this. Most companies spending this much are too slow to hand decisions to agents, and most companies that would let you are too small to give the agents anything to decide. Here you get both, and nobody has written the playbook yet.

 

What you'll build

Horizon 1: Master the engine (first 90 days)

  • Own the numbers: run the weekly read of the acquisition funnel (spend, leads, qualified sellers, booked calls, expected margin per call) vs plan. Explain every gap down to its root cause and drive the actions that close it.

  • Make the data trustworthy: build the single source of truth with our Data team, set the counting and attribution rules, and own the conversion signals we send to Meta, Google and every new platform, including how we count and value bookings made by our AI sales agent as it takes over the qualification call.

  • Find the first levers: landing pages, keyword quality, creative performance, base activation, new channels. Ship fast, measure honestly.

Horizon 2: Automate the loop (months 3 to 9)

  • Agents that see: automated monitoring, anomaly detection and daily variance diagnosis, so problems are caught in hours, not weeks.

  • Agents that decide: explicit, testable rules and models for budget allocation, creative cut and scale, bidding signals and activation timing.

  • Agents that act: campaign changes, CRM activations and experiments executed automatically within guardrails, with humans approving what matters.

Horizon 3: Scale the autopilot (9 months and beyond)

  • Close the loop between creative, media, CRM and our AI sales agent, so every learning flows back into every channel.

  • Run experimentation on autopilot: hypotheses generated, tests launched, results read and rolled out continuously.

  • Define the operating model of a growth team where agents do the execution and people do the thinking, and grow the team that runs it.

 

Why this role

  • Impact you can measure in euros: every decision you make moves expected margin, and you'll see it within days.

  • Build, don't advise: you'll ship agents, models and automations, not recommendations. You get frontier AI tools, our data platform and engineers who build with you.

  • Direct line to leadership: you'll present growth performance every week and shape decisions at company level.

  • A rare combination: strategy, data, marketing and AI engineering in a single seat. The steepest learning curve we can offer.

  • A path that grows with the system: from operator to architect to leader of growth automation at Zefir.

 

Who you are

  • Top-tier problem solver: 2 to 6 years at a top strategy consultancy (BCG, McKinsey, Bain...), in Growth, Ops or Strategy at a high-growth tech company, or both. You structure messy problems in minutes and you get the math right the first time.

  • Builder at heart: you have already built something real: a model, a tool, an automation, an AI agent, a side project. SQL is second nature; Python is a strong plus. You'd rather prototype in an afternoon than debate for a week.

  • Commercial instinct: you think in revenue, not in vanity metrics. You're curious about why people click, book and buy, and you know when fewer leads is good news.

  • Systems thinker: when you see a task done twice, you design the system that removes it. You care about guardrails, feedback loops and what happens when things break.

  • Ownership and clarity: you hold a high bar, move fast and own outcomes. You write crisp updates that start with the number, the cause and the action.

  • Languages: fluency in French and English is required.

  • What we don't require: years of media buying or a marketing title. We hire for slope, not intercept: if you learn fast and build relentlessly, we'll teach you the rest.

  • 30-min call with our Talent Lead

  • 30-min interview with the hiring manager

  • 60-min live case on real (anonymised) funnel data. AI is allowed in part of the case: we want to see how you use it.

  • Swile meal card: €11 per worked day.

  • Swile mobility card: €45/month to support sustainable transportation (metro, carpooling, biking…).

  • Team events: Monthly Mixers to connect and share good times, and quarterly All Hands to celebrate wins across the company.

Our Operating Principles

🏔️ Steep Mountains Are Steep: Setting ambitious goals and working hard to achieve them.

🌊 Ride Reality: Actively seeking challenges and thriving by adapting flexibly to changes.

Claap is the AI-native Revenue Intelligence platform for sales and revenue teams.

- Positively impacted the company's revenue through solutions you've helped launch

- Influenced the Claap product vision by suggesting transformative developments

- A founding role: you're the first PM at Claap, with real ownership on a fast-growing AI product and a direct line to the founders

- A chance to work with an innovative, fast-paced team with a bias for action

    Aqua Swim Academy est une école de natation pour enfants et adultes présente autour du Lac Léman, notamment à Genève, Coppet, Lausanne, Montreux et Aubonne. Nous proposons des cours tout au long de l'année ainsi que des camps pendant les vacances scolaires. Notre mission : faire progresser chaque nageur dans l'eau, avec plaisir et en confiance.

    Pour accompagner notre développement, nous recherchons une personne polyvalente qui contribuera à la fois à la communication de notre marque et à l'accueil des familles.

    Vos missions

    Communication & marketing

    • Créer des contenus pour nos réseaux sociaux (Instagram, Facebook et LinkedIn) : photos, vidéos et stories.

    • Participer à la préparation de la newsletter et des campagnes d'inscription.

    • Réaliser des reportages et couvrir nos événements : portes ouvertes, camps et compétitions.

    • Suivre les statistiques de communication et proposer des idées pour développer notre communauté.

    Accueil & relation familles

    • Accueillir les familles et les nageurs lors des journées de cours et des camps, et veiller à ce que tout se passe bien sur place.

    • Faire le lien entre les familles, les coachs et l'équipe : répondre aux questions, transmettre les retours.

    • Contribuer à une expérience client chaleureuse et soignée, du premier cours aux événements.

    Votre profil

    • Vous suivez une formation en communication ou en marketing.

    • Vous êtes à l'aise dans la relation client, accueillant·e, organisé·e et doté·e d'un bon sens du service.

    • Vous êtes créatif·ve et maîtrisez les réseaux sociaux et les outils de création de contenu.

    • Vous avez un niveau de français parfait et un excellent niveau d'anglais. Une autre langue constitue un atout.

    • Vous appréciez le sport et l'univers de la natation.

    Ce que nous vous offrons

    • Des responsabilités concrètes et une expérience professionnalisante au quotidien.

    • Une vision globale du fonctionnement d'une entreprise sportive en développement, entre opérations, relation client et marketing.

    • Une équipe jeune, dynamique et internationale.

    • L'opportunité de participer activement à des projets variés et de proposer vos propres idées.

    Conditions du stage

    • Lieu : Genève (Acacias), avec des déplacements ponctuels sur nos différents sites.

    • Début : dès que possible.

    • Durée : dès 4 mois.

    • Taux d'activité : à définir.

    • Convention : stage conventionné, une convention de stage est obligatoire.

    • Rémunération : stage non rémunéré.

    Think about what Revolut did to banking. All of the complexity (the regulation, the clearing, the compliance) handled invisibly in the background, and one simple experience at the front.     One platform means one frontend. One experience means it looks and behaves like quinn whether you are in Zurich or in London, a household or a company. In this strategy that is not a nice-to-have. It is the strategy.

    Today, quinn runs on several separate web apps: one per product and market, each with its own frontend, grown over the years as the company grew. Our backend engineers built them alongside everything else, plus an internal admin tool that grew the same way. They all work: thousands of employers run payroll through them every month. But nobody was ever tasked with owning the frontend development, so each one got built the way frontend is built by Backend Developers, seen as a hassle rather than the main aspect users interactive with.

    Auditors sign their name to every conclusion. An agent can do the heavy lifting, but only if the auditor can see how each conclusion was reached and trace it back to its source.

    Agent Builder is where firms turn their own procedures into agents their whole team can run, in Alwin by DataSnipper, our agentic automation platform for audit and finance. Built well, an agent makes quality a property of the procedure, not of who happened to be staffed on the engagement.

    You'll own Agent Builder and the agents firms build with it. Your users are the people at firms who build agents, and the methodology and quality teams who approve them for client work.

    This is a technical PM role. You'll shape the harness each agent runs in: the context it sees, the tools it uses, and where a person reviews its work.     About DataSnipper

    The hardest AI problems aren't about getting an answer fast. They're about getting one people can trust.

    We believe trust is essential to how society works. Every day, we rely on information that's been independently verified, from financial statements to the products we buy, to the sustainability claims companies make. Behind that trust are audit and finance professionals who examine evidence, verify information and hold organizations accountable.

    At DataSnipper, we build AI solutions that empower those professionals. By making evidence easier to trace and verify, we help them focus on the judgment and expertise that make their work so important.

    For our product and engineering team, this is where things get exciting. In audit, a plausible answer isn't good enough. Every output has to be explainable and traceable back to its source. We've just launched a brand new agentic platform, Alwin by DataSnipper. AI agents running in the cloud across hundreds of documents at once, reasoning across PDF, Word and Excel, with a full audit trail behind every step. There are lots of greenfield problems ahead, and real room to shape what we build and how we build it.

Backed by a $100 million Series B led by Index Ventures, at a $1 billion valuation, and as proud members of 1% for the Planet, we care about how we grow, not just how fast.

    If you want to build AI that professionals trust with work that really matters, this is your chance to help shape the future of audit and finance and do the best work of your career along the way.

    The problems you'll own

    • A firm's procedure must become a harness an agent can follow, with the right context, tools and review points

    • Models are non-deterministic, but audit work must be defensible: traceable, attributed and reviewed

    • A firm will only rely on an agent it can test, approve and trace

    • Reviewer feedback must make agents better, with the firm's approval and without anything reaching another client

    • Methodology, models and standards all change. Agents in use must keep up without breaking work in progress

    What you'll do

    • Own the Agent Builder strategy and roadmap, and make the trade-offs explicit

    • Design the harness with engineering: how context is assembled, how tools are defined and called, and where a person must review

    • Decide what builders control and what the platform sets, so agents can encode real methodology and stay consistent

    • Build the feedback loops: turn run traces and reviewer edits into eval cases, regression tests and changes the firm approves

    • Set the quality gates an agent must pass before release, and test every new model or methodology version before it reaches live work

    • Report agent quality with a stated method and sample

    • Prototype in code before you write specs. Then write short specs and decision memos that engineers can build from

    • Spend time with the firms that build and approve agents, and turn what our forward-deployed teams learn into product, not one-off fixes

    What you bring

    • A technical background: software, ML or infrastructure engineering, or several years as a technical PM on developer or AI platforms

    • Hands-on experience shipping agent systems in production: context and retrieval, tool calling, orchestration, structured outputs, retries and fallbacks

    • Eval practice: building datasets, calibrating LLM judges against human labels, offline and online evaluation, and regression testing across model versions

    • Observability for LLM systems: traces, cost and latency, and classifying failures so you fix causes, not symptoms

    • System design skills: schemas, versioning, permissions, event logs and APIs. You can read a design doc and challenge it

    • PM experience on a product that other people build on

    • Prototyping in code with AI tools as part of your normal work

    • Clear, short writing

    • Audit or accounting knowledge, from practice or from building products for auditors, finance teams or other experts in regulated fields

    • Document AI: extraction, OCR, grounding and citation

    Get to Know Us

    Horizon3.ai is a fast-growing, remote cybersecurity company dedicated to the mission of enabling organisations to proactively find and fix and verify exploitable attack vectors before criminals exploit them. Our flagship product, the NodeZeroTM platform, delivers production-safe autonomous pentests and other key assessment operations that scale across the largest internal, external, cloud, and hybrid cloud environments. NodeZero has been adopted by organisations of all sizes, from small educational institutions to government agencies and Global 100 enterprises. It is used by ITOps/SecOps teams, consulting pentesters, and MSSPs and MSPs.

    We are a fusion of former U.S. Special Operations cyber operators, startup engineers, and formerly frustrated cybersecurity practitioners. We're committed to helping solve our common security problems: ineffective security tools, false positives resulting in alert fatigue, blind spots, "checkbox” security culture, cybersecurity skills shortage, and the long lead time and expense of hiring outside consultants. Collectively, we are a team of learn it alls, committed to a culture of respect, collaboration, ownership, and results.

    Role Description

    Help shape the next stage of Horizon3.ai’s META growth. Based in the Netherlands with regular travel to the region, you’ll bring autonomous pentesting to new customers and help them reduce real-world security risk. If you thrive on opening doors, building partnerships and turning opportunities into wins, this is a chance to make a visible impact as we expand our META Commercial team.

    We currently require our Amsterdam team to come to the office 2 - 3 days per week.

    What You’ll Do

    Grow Horizon3.ai’s META Commercial business by winning new customers, developing productive channel partnerships and helping organisations realise value from our cybersecurity solutions.

    • Win new accounts and expand our customer base by introducing disruptive cybersecurity software solutions to the META market.

    • Build and convert a qualified pipeline, owning the sales cycle from qualification and proof of value through negotiation and close, with the goal of exceeding quota consistently quarter over quarter.

    • Turn channel partnerships into revenue by proactively engaging regional resellers and developing joint opportunities.

    • Demonstrate Horizon3.ai solutions in virtual and in-person meetings, connecting technical capabilities to customer needs and business outcomes.

    • Drive the post-proof of value ROI process, helping customers understand business value while building relationships that support satisfaction and retention.

    • Maintain accurate customer records, pipeline data and forecasts in Salesforce so opportunities, risks and next steps are clearly understood.

    • Work independently to progress opportunities while collaborating with distributed sales, support and customer success teams to deliver a coordinated customer experience.

    What You’ll Bring

    • At least 3-5 years of successful cybersecurity sales experience, with a track record of driving growth, introducing disruptive software solutions and consistently exceeding quarterly quotas.

    • Previous experience selling technical solutions into the META region.

    • Experience establishing and monetising channel partnerships; existing relationships with key regional resellers are essential.

    • Proficiency across the full sales process, including qualification, proof of value, forecasting, negotiation, deal closure and post-proof of value ROI management.

    • The ability to present and demonstrate cybersecurity solutions effectively, both virtually and in person.

    • Strong CRM discipline and experience maintaining accurate pipeline records and forecasts in Salesforce (SFDC).

    • Familiarity with Challenger Question-Based Selling-type methodologies and sales tools such as Outreach, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, ZoomInfo and Slack.

    • The ability to work independently and collaborate effectively with distributed teams.

    • Fluency in English and Arabic; additional language skills such as French are welcomed.

    Travel Required

    We are a hybrid company, and this job will require you to spend 3 days based at our Amsterdam city centre sales hub. The role may require up to 40% of travel within the assigned territory to be successful. Job-related travel expenses are reviewed and must be approved by your manager.

    Perks of Horizon3.ai

    • Inclusive Team: We value diversity and promote an inclusive culture where everyone can thrive.

    • Growth Opportunities: Be part of a dynamic and growing team with numerous career development opportunities.

    • Innovative Culture: Work in a collaborative environment that encourages creativity and out-of-the-box thinking.

    • Remote Work: We are a 100% remote company. Enjoy the flexibility to work in the way that supports you and brings out your best.

    • Competitive Compensation: We offer competitive salary, equity and benefits. Our benefits include health, vision & dental insurance for you and your family, a flexible vacation policy, and generous parental leave.

    You Belong Here

    Horizon3.ai is not just an equal opportunity employer - we are a community that values diversity, equity, and inclusion as fundamental principles of our culture and success. We are dedicated to fostering a workplace where everyone feels welcome and respected, regardless of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, hair length or any other legally protected status by law.

    Our commitment to diversity and inclusion means we strive to attract, develop, and retain a workforce that reflects the varied communities we serve. We believe that diverse perspectives drive innovation and strengthen our ability to create cutting-edge cybersecurity solutions. At Horizon3.ai, every team member is valued and supported in an environment that encourages personal and professional growth.

    We welcome candidates from all backgrounds and experiences, and we encourage all qualified individuals to apply. Come be a part of Horizon3.ai, where your unique contributions are recognized, and your potential is limitless.

Some of these benefits include:</span><span data-ccp-props="{"134233117":true,"134233118":true,"201341983":0,"335559738":200,"335559739":0,"335559740":240}"> </span></span></h3> <ul> <li data-leveltext="" data-font="Symbol" data-listid="33" data-list-defn-props="{"335552541":1,"335559685":720,"335559991":360,"469769226":"Symbol","469769242":[8226],"469777803":"left","469777804":"","469777815":"multilevel"}" data-aria-posinset="1" data-aria-level="1"><span data-contrast="none">Generous Annual Leave Policy:</span><span data-contrast="none"> We recognise everyone needs a well-deserved break. In addition to this, we have introduced our 5-Year Recharge benefit which allows all employees an additional 2 weeks of paid leave after 5 years continuous service.</span><span data-ccp-props="{"134233117":true,"134233118":true,"201341983":2,"335559685":1320,"335559738":200,"335559739":0,"335559740":240}"> </span></li> </ul> <ul> <li data-leveltext="" data-font="Symbol" data-listid="33" data-list-defn-props="{"335552541":1,"335559685":720,"335559991":360,"469769226":"Symbol","469769242":[8226],"469777803":"left","469777804":"","469777815":"multilevel"}" data-aria-posinset="2" data-aria-level="1"><span data-contrast="none">Flexible Working:</span><span data-contrast="none"> We know that the ‘ideal’ work-life balance will vary from person to person and change at different stages of our working lives.     Can you help us fix the world's most broken supply chain?

    The fashion industry produces over 100 billion garments a year. 60% end up in landfill, not because people don't want these clothes, but because the supply chain that moves them from donation to resale is offline, manual and broken.

    Fleek is fixing this. Our mission is to make secondhand the first choice. We run a B2B marketplace where resellers and stores buy clothing in bulk, and we build the AI systems that digitise the supply chain behind it.

    Our buyers sell on eBay, Vinted, Depop, Whatnot, eBay Live and TikTok Shop, or run vintage stores from Brick Lane to Paris to New York. They source graded stock from wholesalers and rag houses across many countries. Our key enabler is FleekSort, an AI model fine-tuned on secondhand fashion that can grade, price and categorise an item from a single photo.

    We are now going well beyond vintage. Live sellers can sell almost anything, and there is an opportunity for Fleek to be the backend for B2B resale. We've now started onboarding customers alongside supply from Japan, South Korea, the Philippines and Thailand.

    Since 2022, we've saved 9 million items from landfill and tripled in size year on year. We've raised ~$50M from a16z, Y Combinator, HV Capital and others, and recently closed our Series B. Our advisors and private investors include operators behind Depop, Shopify and Postmates.

    We're looking for people who want to build something that matters, and move fast doing it.

    About the role

    You'll join the GTM team as our GTM Engineer, reporting to our GTM lead and working day to day with the new business team. You'll own the system we use to find and win customers, on both sides of the marketplace.

    On the demand side, that means online resellers, live sellers and physical stores in the UK, Europe and the US, buying vintage, deadstock, new with tags and luxury. On the supply side, it means the brands, brokers, wholesalers and rag houses who sell to them. As we add new categories and markets, the system has to find those customers too.

    We already have pipelines that scrape marketplaces and load leads into our CRM. The next step is everything after that: putting the right leads first, reaching them well, and learning from every outcome. You'll own the engine end to end, from the first scrape to the revenue each new customer brings in.

    This is not a typical B2B SaaS GTM engineering role. You won't spend your days wiring a CRM to a LinkedIn sequencer or building dashboards. Everyone on our commercial team builds their own tools with AI. You'll take on the problems they can't: systems that improve themselves, infrastructure that scales, and outreach that works within limits set by platforms like Meta.

    The role is part engineer, part product manager and part commercial. You won't carry a closes target, but you'll own every metric that moves it.

    The problem you'll solve

    We want a system that finds the right customers, puts them in order, reaches out, and gets better every week. It runs as a loop:

    1. Find. Source leads across marketplaces and social platforms, for every segment and market we sell into.

    2. Prioritise. Score each lead on the signals that predict a good customer, not just a likely reply.

    3. Reach out. Contact them on Instagram, WhatsApp, email, phone or LinkedIn, personalised by AI and handed to a rep at the right moment.

    4. Learn. Feed every outcome back into scoring. If a store replied but wasn't a fit, similar leads drop down the list, so we stop spending tokens and rep time on them. Then back to step 1.

    To make that loop work, you'll build a second brain for GTM: one layer that holds everything we know about a customer, with models and agents running on top. That includes the messages we sent and how they replied, how fast they replied and closed, what they sell and where, what they click and search for in our app, what they told our reps on calls, and how much they spend and how well they retain.

    The same data powers our account management team, who look after customers once they've placed their first orders. Matching each buyer with the right supply is one of their next big problems, and you'll help solve it.

    What you'll do

    • Own the acquisition engine. Learn how our current pipelines work and improve them. If a rebuild is the right call, make the case for it, and keep leads flowing to the reps while you build.

    • Source at scale in new segments. Find vintage stores, live sellers, deadstock and luxury buyers, and new suppliers, in every market we enter.

    • Build the scoring and feedback loop. Define what a good lead looks like for each segment, then keep refining it on what actually closes and what actually spends.

    • Engineer multi-channel outreach. Instagram, WhatsApp, email, calls and LinkedIn, personalised by AI and built around real limits like Instagram DM caps and Meta restrictions.

    • Own the funnel numbers. Leads sourced per day on each platform, reply rate, conversion rate and GMV per close by source. Use them to decide what to fix next.

    • Sit with the reps and talk to customers. Learn why a lead is good and how each segment wants to be sold to. Then automate the repetitive parts of the rep's day.

    • Turn repeat work into agents. Qualification, first messages, reply handling, dedupe and CRM hygiene should run without a person.

    • Keep it efficient. Every system you build should make sense on cost per lead and unit economics.

    • Connect acquisition to retention. Make sure new customers land cleanly with account management, and help build the buyer-to-supply matching they rely on.

    What you bring

    • A strong technical background. You've built and run real systems, such as data pipelines, scrapers, models or production infrastructure. You've done more than configure tools.

    • An AI-first mindset, a step ahead. You build with Claude and other models every day and know where agents work and where they break. Our commercial team is very AI-literate, and you'll push them further.

    • Curiosity about the customer. You want to know why one lead closes and another doesn't, and how each segment wants to be sold to. You're happy on a call with a reseller.

    • Problem solving over playbooks. You take an ambiguous problem, form your own view and ship something that works. We'd rather hire someone who works it out than someone repeating what worked elsewhere.

    • Ownership. You challenge how things are done, bring your own recommendations and explain why.

    • Rigour with numbers. You track honest metrics, know where your funnel leaks and judge your systems on results.

    • Excitement about the space. You see how big the opportunity is and want to build it.

    Nice to have

    • GTM, growth or RevOps experience, including outbound you've run yourself

    • Founder or early-startup experience where you owned growth end to end

    • Experience building ranking, scoring or recommendation models

    • Experience building for marketplaces, resellers, live selling or independent retail

    • Familiarity with secondhand, vintage, deadstock or luxury fashion

    • Running multi-channel outbound under platform limits (DM caps, deliverability, warm-up)

    What good looks like

    • First 30 days: you know the current pipelines inside out, have sat with the reps and have shipped your first improvements, with leads still flowing. You've shared your plan to improve what's there or rebuild it, and why.

    • 3 months: one data layer joins outreach, replies, closes, app activity, call notes and spend. Scoring runs on it, and the loop from outcome back to scoring is live for at least one segment.

    • 6 months: the system improves itself. Each week it sources more leads, and better ones, across our segments and markets, and conversion and GMV per close are rising.

    • 12 months: the engine is the backbone of acquisition across vintage, deadstock and luxury, on both demand and supply. Agents run the repeat work, and you focus on what to build next.

    What you'll get

    • Competitive salary plus a performance bonus tied to qualified pipeline

    • Generous equity: being on Fleek means you'll own a part of it

    • Comprehensive healthcare coverage

    • A collaborative team in a lovely office in the heart of East London

    • Access to founders. We're a small team and they're heavily involved (and good fun!)

    • Exclusive employee discounts to buy on Fleek

    • Access to borrow any item from our collection of vintage and reworks in the office

    • A disproportionate level of responsibility and the chance to drive massive impact

    How we work

    High ownership, non-hierarchical and fast-moving. We hire problem solvers, not order takers. If you have a better way to do something, and it moves the numbers at a sensible cost, go for it.

    Our commercial team builds its own tools, so each new hire starts more effective than the last. People who deliver get more scope quickly. You'll work embedded with the GTM team, ship fast and see your work in the pipeline within days, not quarters.

    The practicalities

    • Location: London HQ, E1, Spitalfields / Shoreditch

    • Work model: in person, with trust-based flexibility

    • Stage: post-Series B, hyper-growth

    • Team: a GTM team of 5 AEs in new business and 3 AMs in account management, within 100+ people across London, India and Pakistan

    • Process: an intro call, then an in-person case study in two parts: one on the business with our GTM lead, one technical with our engineers

    Our values

    Five values shape how we work at Fleek:

    • Dream Big and Disrupt Yourself: Push the most ambitious version of what you're building. Step out of your comfort zone. Nothing is out of reach.

    • Absolute Ownership: The buck stops with you. Drive initiatives to completion. Experiment, learn, persevere. The job isn't done until the job is done.

    • Curiosity Leads the Way: Don't accept anything at face value. Ask questions you don't know the answer to. That's how you innovate.

    • Talk to the Customer: Deeply understand their challenges, motivations and ambitions. Every decision starts with the customer at the centre.

    • Embrace Diversity: A global team building for a global supply chain. Bring your authentic self and embrace the diversity of everyone you encounter.

    Ready to build the infrastructure for the world's fastest-growing fashion economy? If you want to work on genuinely hard problems, with a world-class team, at a company that's tripling annually, we'd love to hear from you.

    Health can’t wait.

    You will be part of the Business Strategy & Operations (BSO) team, whose goal is to

    • Define an ambitious strategy to achieve our business objectives and translate this into an actionable plan

    • Monitor and explain our performance towards our business objectives

    • Enable our Sales and Account Management teams to achieve these business objectives and become the most effective commercial teams in the tech industry (i.e., Sales and AM effectiveness, tools, analytics and training)

    Across all these areas we work very closely with the Senior Leadership, the Sales, Account Management and Go-to-Market teams. The scope is Global (France, Belgium, Spain and Canada for the time being).

    🎯 Your mission

    You will be owning medium to large scale/complexity projects (depending on your skills and experience) on the Business Planning and Strategy area. These would include:

    • Business Strategy

      • Work closely with senior business leaders (Business leads, Insurance Lead, Marketing lead, CFO, CEO, etc.) to define Alan’s business plan

      • Frame business and resource allocation decisions (e.g. where to accelerate/slow down in terms of segments or products, where to deploy sales and marketing resources, how to optimize for short vs. long term, what are is the impact on metrics such as payback, LTV, CAC)

      • Propose adjustments to the plan on a quarterly basis and support Board preparation

    • Sales & Account Manager Planning

      • Translate the plan into actionable sales & Account Management objectives, ensuring their quality, scalability and accuracy

      • Build & improve the infrastructure to track these targets (dashboard, models) hand in hand with the data team

    • Performance monitoring & Steering

      • Lead or support strategic explorations (e.g. new segment, new distribution models) to frame strategic decisions

      • Monitor closely results and execution to gather learnings and adjust where necessary, sharing key learnings with the community and the company on a monthly basis

      • Work on transversal topics that allow us to gain insights & better steer the team performance (competition analysis, implementation & monitoring of pricing strategies, ...)

    🧐 Skills we are looking for

    We look above all for exceptional people motivated and committed in building one of the most effective Strategy and Planning team.

    At least 3 years of experience within either:

    • Business strategy, sales strategy & operations, revenue operations or business finance/ strategic finance departments in a B2B company (preferably)

    • Management consulting, investment banking or private equity

    Critical thinking and problem solving skills:

    • Ability to deal effectively with ambiguity, bringing structure to ambiguous areas of opportunity

    • Deep analytical rigour, bringing clarity on complex topics through deep insights

    • Great Excel skills and moderate SQL knowledge. Experience with AI tools and building moderate to complex flows.

    • Ability to handle workload & short turnaround time, with a high degree of adaptability and flexibility, when some topics are top priority for the company

    Business sense:

    • At ease with B2B operational and financial metrics

    • Passion for getting close to the business and Sales/Marketing teams and understanding the operational details of their work, not just the strategic ones

    Communication and presence:

    • Ability to communicate effectively with senior leadership and align multiple stakeholders in a collaborative way

    • Ability to build successful relationships with a broad range of stakeholders across Sales, Marketing, Product and Finance and be seen as a trusted contributor/advisor

    • Ability to work well under pressure, with a high degree of adaptability and flexibility

    • Great written and oral structure and communication

    • Fluency in English (French is a strong plus)

    • Being based in (or willing to relocate to) the Paris or Barcelona area

    Nice to have

    • Experience with BI and visualization tools (Metabase, Tableau) and Salesforce

    • Experience in the SaaS/Tech sectors

    • Exposure to large sales teams (100+)

    For this opportunity, we are aiming to hire within the C1-D level range.

    Therefore, we offer:

    • Fair rewards. Generous equity packages complement your base salary.

    • Flexible Office. Amazing office space at our Paris HQ or Barcelona office

    • Flexible vacation policy and flexible working hours. organize your time as you wish.

    • Delightful healthcare insurance: Extremely comprehensive health insurance - 100% for you and your children, 90-100% for partners depending on your country (permanent contracts only).

    • Transport. Country-specific commuter benefits.

    • Learning & Training opportunities. A highly flexible Training policy free books and budget to attend and speak at conferences if the opportunity arises.

    • Personal growth through coaching: At Alan, coaching isn't just a perk - ****it's core to who we are.     • Parental leave. Extended parental leave for all new parents.

    About us

    Owkin is an agentic AI company pioneering Biological Artificial Superintelligence to solve problems in biology where human researchers alone have failed.
    Owkin builds K Pro - an AI scientist for pharmaceutical research and strategic decision-making. K Pro orchestrates a suite of AI skills and tools to decode complex biology, accelerate research, and dramatically increase productivity.
    K Pro is built on Owkin’s unrivalled multimodal patient data network, state-of-the-art AI for biology and a decade of experience working with pharmaceutical partners.

    Position is based in our Paris office or remotely in France, UK or Germany.

    Please submit your CV in English

    About the role:

    Owkin is looking for a Customer Support Specialist to own first-level support for K-Pro, Owkin's AI research platform for biopharma R&D, used by AstraZeneca, Sanofi, Servier and Boehringer Ingelheim.

    Our clients have made major investments to access K-Pro, and their contracts come with strict response and resolution SLAs. You will be their first point of contact during business hours: the person who understands their problem quickly, keeps them informed, and gets the right engineering, product or customer success people moving. You will also help shape how support works at Owkin, including where AI and agentisation make it better.

     

    In particular, you will:

    Own the support flow

    • Own incoming tickets during business hours as the first line of support for all K-Pro clients

    • Triage every ticket: set priority (P1 to P4) and the impacted service, and route it to the right team

    • Keep SLAs on track: follow up on open tickets, escalate early when a deadline is at risk

    • Communicate clear, timely updates to users and CSMs throughout the ticket lifecycled 

     Go deep on the product

    • Diagnose issues directly with users: reproduce bugs, check data and configurations, and give engineers a clean, actionable report

    • Learn K-Pro in depth (its features, the datasets clients use, how login, API access, exports and permissions work, and the research questions clients bring to it) so you can resolve most issues without escalating

    • Recognise when a result looks scientifically wrong and when it's a usage question

    Turn support into insight

    • Act as the Customer Success team's eyes on support: flag critical tickets, recurring issues, and signs that a client is becoming dissatisfied, so CSMs can act early

    • Spot patterns across tickets and turn them into product feedback, doc updates or process fixes

    • Track and report on support metrics (response time, SLA compliance, first contact resolution, volume) and give actionable insights to the team.

    Own the knowledge base

    • Own the K-Pro help center: write, update and remove articles as new issues are resolved

    • Turn one-off fixes into reusable answers for clients and for the support team

    Improve support with AI

    • Identify where automation and AI tools (triage, routing, response drafting, knowledge retrieval) would save time or improve quality

    • Work with R&Tech Operations to build, test and improve these workflows

     

    About you

    Required qualifications / experience:

    • Proven technical support or customer support for B2B software, ideally SaaS, with enterprise clients

    • A track record handling SLA-bound support with demanding customers, and staying calm under pressure

    • Strong technical curiosity: comfortable with APIs, logs, data and configurations; basic SQL or scripting is a plus

    • Hands-on experience with AI tooling and building or improving agentic support workflows (AI-assisted triage, automated routing, LLM-powered drafting), and the judgment to know when automation fits

    • Excellent written and verbal communication, able to explain technical issues to scientists and to engineers alike

    • Experience with support tooling such as Zendesk, Linear and PagerDuty, or equivalent

    • Able to follow runbooks and escalation paths, and to know when to deviate from them

    • A habit of turning fixes into documentation and patterns into insights

    Preferred qualifications/bonus:

    • Experience in life sciences, biopharma or another regulated industry is a strong plus

    What success looks like in your first 6 months

    • You handle the full ticket flow for all K-Pro clients with SLAs met

    • CSMs rely on your signals to anticipate account risks

    • The help center covers the most frequent ticket types

    • You have shipped at least one automation that measurably improves support

    • Lead and coach your team: run daily regional support operations including prioritization and resourcing, hold regular team meetings and career growth conversations, and build a culture where people feel supported and excited to grow.

    • Based in the Zurich area, or willing to relocate, and able to work on-site in our Zurich office Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday.

Along the way, you define how system and module upgrades are managed through the BOM.

    You become the single point of contact for master data and change implementation. You make sure every build uses the correct released configuration, so that each Device History Record traces back to the Device Master Record.
